strategy.sub_strategy: Credit relative value / cross-asset convexity
strategy.description: Discretionary relative value strategy seeking to capture price inefficiencies across credit, equity and derivatives markets. The fund focuses predominantly on US instruments with some European exposure, targeting dislocations within credit (corporate bonds, CDS, structured credit tranches) and across asset classes (credit vs. equity vs. volatility). Core philosophy is to build structurally convex trade profiles with limited or no negative carry, using instruments including bonds, CDS, CDX tranches, equity options, OTC derivatives (variance swaps, dispersion, FVAs), and VIX products. Portfolio holds an average of 100-150 trades with 1-10 legs each (typically 2: 1 long, 1 short), holding period 3 months to 1 year. Strong bias to be long quality/liquid and short lower quality/less liquid instruments. Dynamic allocation across four sub-strategies: Corporate Credit RV, Debt/Equity, Structured Credit, and Volatility. Targets double-digit returns through the cycle with limited downside risk and low correlation to traditional risk premiums.
strategy.investment_thesis_core: Exploits structural mispricings between credit, equity and volatility markets that arise from investor segmentation, regulatory constraints on banks, dominance of long-biased mutual funds, and the retreat of prop trading desks since 2008. Convexity is engineered at the trade level by finding instruments that exhibit asymmetric payoff profiles, allowing the fund to make more in favorable scenarios than it loses in adverse ones, without relying on directional market calls.
strategy.idea_generation: Proprietary systematic screens covering 15,000 bonds/loans, 700 CDS, 2,500 equities, 2,000 volatility instruments, and 3,300 financials. Screens generate basis reports, curve reports, debt-equity reports, tranche reports, and volatility reports. Complemented by thematic/fundamental research and broker-dealer relationships. Continuous monitoring of market dynamics, sector flows, and new issue calendar. Business cycle framework guides top-down thematic biases across four phases (Reflation, Inflation, Stagflation, Deflation).
strategy.neutrality_approach: Market neutral bias; most trades structured in relative value framework close to market and factor neutral
strategy.family_defining_note: Strategy is defined by engineered convexity at the trade level across credit, equity, and volatility instruments; four sub-strategies (Corporate Credit RV, Debt/Equity, Structured Credit, Volatility) are dynamically allocated.

risk_framework.risk_framework_description: Risk management is integrated into portfolio construction at the trade level. Most trades are structured in a relative value framework close to market neutral with positive convexity. Diversification across 100+ trades is a key risk management tool; each trade sized so stress scenario loss is limited to 100bp contribution. Risk metrics monitored in real-time via Enfusion and MSCI RiskMetrics, with particular focus on stress scenarios given nonlinearity of many products. Hard limits include: jump-to-default exposure limited to 5% per HY name and 10% per IG name; portfolio drawdown limits (soft and hard); hard stop for any idea if historical contribution to losses reaches 2%; 10-day VaR limit at 5%. Volatility target of 6% with maximum ex-ante volatility of 8%. Peak-to-trough drawdown restriction of 15%. Overlay hedging used when attractive, typically in option format, costing on average 1-2% per year.
risk_framework.drawdown_response_protocol: Portfolio drawdown limits (soft and hard) are monitored daily. Hard stop triggered if any individual idea's historical contribution to losses reaches 2%. Risk reduction begins with pre-trade analysis and position sizing. CRO has authority to enforce risk reduction or liquidation if portfolio manager and risk manager disagree after limit breach.

strategy.sub_strategy: Off-the-Run Middle-Market Stressed Credit
strategy.description: 2E Capital Partners invests in performing stressed corporate debt of middle-market companies in North America, focusing on under-followed, out-of-favor, or off-the-run situations where the firm believes it has an analytical edge. The strategy targets companies with enterprise values of $1-5B, primarily investing in first lien bank loans and high yield bonds in the secondary market, with a long bias (target net exposure 90-95%) and episodic single-name alpha shorts (5-10% of portfolio). The portfolio holds 25-30 long positions with core positions at 2-4% of NAV at cost, maximum 7.5% per issuer, and maximum 15% per industry. The strategy targets five opportunity buckets: Post-LME Super-Senior Debt (~30%), Post-Reorganization Performing Takeback Debt (~22.75%), LME Stubs (~15%), Situational Investments (~27.25%), and Single-Name Alpha Shorts (~5.25%). Target total return is 13-15% over the cycle with a focus on capital preservation and contracted returns through interest and principal amortization. No leverage is used; the fund uses prime brokers for trading and custody only.
strategy.investment_thesis_core: Exploits structural inefficiency in the North American middle-market stressed credit space, where larger managers have migrated to illiquid or large-cap opportunities, leaving a persistent opportunity set of mispriced first lien debt in companies with good businesses but bad capital structures, particularly post-LME situations and catalyst-driven pull-to-par trades.
strategy.idea_generation: Sourcing driven by news flow, legal and financial advisers, management teams of portfolio companies, investors, and sell-side research. Weekly review of every issue >$500mn yielding more than 10%; daily tracking of significant yield movers in HY and leveraged loans. Screening focuses on industries in transition, good businesses with poor capital structures, temporary earnings headwinds, liquidity concerns, and post-LME transactions. Full diligence includes boots-on-the-ground research, valuation analysis, channel due diligence, and engagement with competitors, suppliers, customers, and advisors.

strategy.sub_strategy: European equity market-neutral
strategy.description: Fundamental long/short European equity market-neutral strategy targeting uncorrelated alpha from liquid European equities. The portfolio is assembled to maintain near-zero beta, factor, and sector exposures using the proprietary AQUA platform for real-time risk monitoring, portfolio optimisation, and hedging. Idea generation is bottom-up, driven by forensic cash-flow analysis and fundamental research across 1,000 investable European stocks. The long book holds 40+ single-stock positions (1–3% NAV each) and the short book holds 50+ single-stock positions (1–2% NAV each), with a single Euro Stoxx 50 index future used minimally to achieve residual beta neutrality. The strategy targets 5–6% volatility and >5% annualised stock alpha, with a 12–24 month holding period horizon.
strategy.investment_thesis_core: Exploits longer-term (12–24 month) fundamental mispricings in European equities in less-contested alpha pools (balance sheet and intrinsic risk domains), using forensic cash-flow analysis and proprietary AQUA factor-neutralisation to extract idiosyncratic alpha that pod-dominated short-term EPS traders cannot capture.
strategy.idea_generation: AQUA screens 1,000 liquid European stocks generating default valuation models and risk scores. PMs identify promising longs and shorts through fundamental research, feed investment cases into AQUA, which ranks candidates by ratio of expected return to intrinsic risk. PMs select best ideas; AQUA suggests position sizing to optimise portfolio return and risk while achieving zero beta and near-zero factor/sector exposures.

strategy.sub_strategy: Event-driven long/short liquid credit
strategy.description: Alba Credit Opportunities (ACO) is a high-conviction, event-driven (catalyst-driven) long/short credit fund investing globally in liquid corporate and financial debt with a European bias. The strategy focuses exclusively on performing capital structures (sweet spot BBB to B rated issuers) and deliberately avoids distressed credit. Portfolio construction follows a PE-style 'diversified concentration' approach of 20–30 high-conviction positions across bonds and CDS. The Investment Manager decomposes each bond into its risk components (credit spread, interest rate, FX, optionality) and manages each independently via derivatives overlays (IRS, bond futures, single-name CDS, CDX, FX swaps). Catalyst opportunities include M&A, spin-offs, liability management exercises, fallen angels/rising stars, and capital structure dislocations. Net credit exposure is managed via credit index overlays and typically oscillates between -20% and +50% of NAV. Leverage is moderate (target 1.25x–1.75x, max 3.0x). The strategy targets contained volatility below 6% and a net return of 10–12% per annum.
strategy.investment_thesis_core: Exploits wide dispersion within credit ratings bands (e.g., within BBs) driven by idiosyncratic catalysts, while maintaining near-market-neutral credit beta through derivative overlays. The edge lies in deep fundamental credit analysis combined with catalyst identification in performing credit, a niche underserved by both traditional bond funds and distressed-focused hedge funds.
strategy.idea_generation: Ideas sourced via active fundamental research; team participates in equity investor calls to extract information relevant to debt capital structures. strategy.description: AlbaCore employs a flexible hybrid credit mandate investing in European mid-to-large cap performing companies across bespoke private capital solutions (primary unlisted preferred equity, PIK notes, second lien loans) and opportunistic public credit (high yield bonds, leveraged loans below par, bank balance sheet opportunities). The Three Cs investment framework — Credit (margin of safety, large performing companies, free cash flow, ESG), Convexity (OID, fees, call protection, equity kickers/warrants), and Catalyst (refinancing, debt repayment, asset sales, spread tightening, IPO) — drives all investment decisions. The strategy targets mid-to-large cap companies with average EBITDA above €400m, invests across 15+ European countries, and dynamically allocates between private and opportunistic public markets based on relative value. Portfolio holds 30-50 issuers; leverage capped at 25% of aggregate commitments.
strategy.investment_thesis_core: Exploits illiquidity premium and information advantage in European private credit by acting as lead or sole lender in bespoke transactions with limited competition, while opportunistically purchasing mispriced public credit during market dislocations to generate equity-like returns with credit-level downside protection.

market_views.macro_thesis: As of March 2026, AI is fundamentally reshaping corporate economics and credit markets. Software sector faces structural disruption from AI-native alternatives eroding seat-based pricing models, while AI infrastructure build-out (data centres, power, networks) creates compelling opportunities in infrastructure debt. In credit markets, rising dispersion between AI-resilient and AI-vulnerable issuers requires granular bottom-up analysis. Higher-for-longer rates environment (post-2022) has normalised credit spreads and improved risk-adjusted returns in European leveraged finance relative to equities.
sector_views: Software sector faces AI disruption risk; spread widening in 2026 mostly reflects existing credit issues (governance, short maturities, leverage) rather than pure AI exposure; fundamentals of European software issuers broadly healthy but LTVs at risk as equity multiples compress.
Infrastructure debt (data centres, power, grid, fibre) offers compelling opportunities driven by AI capex build-out; long-dated contracted cash flows with strong security packages.
CLO structured credit: single-B tranches under pressure from software/cyclical weakness; BBB and BB tranches offer attractive entry points relative to historical levels.
Senior secured European credit trading near historical recovery values yielding double digits seen as attractive relative to long-term equity returns.
geographic_views: Europe offers higher spreads than US for equivalent credit quality; lower competition and greater jurisdictional complexity support spread premium; lender-on-lender violence rare in Europe vs. US.
European direct lending market growing but less commoditised than US; sub-500bps spreads limited to highest quality credits in Europe.
key_risks_identified: AI disruption to software and business services business models — seat-based pricing erosion.
Higher-for-longer interest rates pressuring leveraged capital structures and refinancing.
Recessionary pressures and sticky inflation in Europe.
Russia/Ukraine geopolitical risk and energy price volatility.
Rising default rates expected in 2023-2024 as refinancing conditions remain challenging.
Equity multiple compression reducing LTV cushions for private credit lenders.
Lender-on-lender violence in US syndicated markets.
market_views.forward_outlook: AlbaCore expects continued dispersion in European credit markets, with AI-resilient businesses (high switching costs, proprietary data, mission-critical products) outperforming. Infrastructure debt platform launched in partnership with MUFG Bank targeting UK/European data centre, power and network financing. Direct lending market expected to remain core financing source for large-cap European companies despite syndicated market recovery.

strategy.sub_strategy: AI-native nonlinear adaptive multi-strategy equity L/S market-neutral
strategy.description: Aleph Invariance deploys a Dual-Engine Framework combining a US Equity Long/Short Core Engine and a Zero-Drag Crisis Alpha Engine. The L/S Core ingests hundreds of linear base factors (Market Dynamics, Positioning, Fundamental/AltData) and expands them into millions of non-linear conditional features via large-scale Deep Learning and a proprietary Conditional MVO framework, targeting idiosyncratic alpha across a universe of ~3,000 US equities (>$250M market cap, ex-HTB). The Crisis Alpha engine is a multi-strategy, multi-asset framework trading 12-24 convex QIS strategies across Macro Momentum, Volatility Defense, Structural Arbitrage, and Equity Micro-Structure pillars via total return swaps sourced from Tier-1 banks. The combined architecture targets a 75/25 L/S Core/Crisis Alpha allocation, a blended Sharpe >3.0, 10-12% volatility, and a hard -10% maximum drawdown structural floor, with leverage dynamically governed by a Dual-Ceiling (Volatility and Stress Capacity) framework. All performance figures are simulated/backtested and not actual fund performance.
strategy.investment_thesis_core: Exploits the mathematical blindness of legacy linear factor models to non-linear conditional probabilities by engineering millions of non-linear features from standard economic primitives, combined with a forward-looking Conditional MVO that predicts optimal portfolio weights rather than prices, enabling a structural 'Variance Cancellation' effect when layered with a zero-carry-cost Crisis Alpha engine.
strategy.idea_generation: Proprietary large-scale Deep Learning signal factory ingests hundreds of linear base factors (Market Dynamics, Positioning, Fundamental/AltData) and expands them into millions of non-linear conditional features across a 2x3 Alpha Matrix (2 Horizons: Daily, Swing x 3 Executions: MOO, VWAP, MOC). Endogenous Transaction Cost Optimization Model treats slippage and borrow as variables inside signal generation. Crisis Alpha engine dynamically sizes 12-24 convex QIS strategies from Tier-1 bank partners using the same Conditional MVO framework.

risk_framework.risk_framework_description: The Invariance Risk Engine governs leverage via a Dual-Ceiling Framework: Gmax = min(Volatility Ceiling, Stress Capacity). The Volatility Ceiling calibrates gearing to normalize ex-ante portfolio volatility to 10-12% using the Axioma Short-Horizon Factor Risk Model. The Stress Capacity calculates maximum leverage such that a Composite Shock (max of 3-sigma tail or historical MDD x 1.5 resilience multiplier, plus a Dynamic Entropy Override scaling 2.0x-4.6x) does not breach the -10% Structural Floor. Hard constraints: >$250M market cap, ex-HTB, 3-Day/15% MDV liquidity protocol, ACTR <0.05% per constituent, Beta 0.0±0.05, Net Exposure 0%±5%.
risk_framework.drawdown_response_protocol: At -5% drawdown, leverage capability is cut by 50% (to 5x from 10x). At -8% drawdown, leverage reduced to 2x. At -10% drawdown, portfolio goes to 1x (unlevered/cash). Leverage recovers proportionally as drawdown recovers. The Dual-Ceiling framework operates as a continuous de-risking curve, not a discrete stop-loss.

strategy.sub_strategy: Beta-neutral long/short Brazilian equities
strategy.description: AlphaKey Long Short is a beta-neutral fund exclusively focused on Brazilian equities, targeting 30-40 long positions and 20-30 short positions. The strategy neutralizes market beta across three dimensions: domestic beta, bond-proxy beta, and commodities beta, aiming for roughly equal risk allocation across these areas. Stock selection is bottom-up and fundamental, focusing on companies with returns above cost of capital, strong earnings growth, sound capital structure, and high governance standards at reasonable multiples. Shorts are single-name alpha trades rather than pairs, selected for flawed business models, excessive optimistic valuations, or inadequate capital structures. The fund targets gross exposure of 60-80% and net exposure of -10% to +10%. Opportunistic positions (max 3% each, max 25% of portfolio) complement core long-term positions. The same underlying research portfolio is shared across all AlphaKey strategies with different sizing.
strategy.investment_thesis_core: Exploits the relative scarcity of long/short managers in Brazil (estimated ~10 practitioners) to generate idiosyncratic alpha on both sides; the short market is less competitive than long-only, providing additional alpha opportunity beyond beta management.
strategy.idea_generation: Quantitative and qualitative screening using multiples and financial metrics, conference attendance, and industry discussions. Investment committee reviews thesis, KPIs, assumptions, risks, and model sensitivity. Analysts cover 20-30 names each across assigned sectors; PMs conduct independent company meetings separate from analysts.

strategy.sub_strategy: Equity Capital Markets (ECM) market-neutral
strategy.description: Transaction-driven, ECM-specialist strategy investing globally in companies undergoing equity capital markets events including IPOs, secondary block offerings, primary capital raises, and follow-on offerings. The long book holds approximately 40-60 positions in ECM-related equities, primarily in Europe, Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, with opportunistic US exposure. strategy.investment_thesis_core: ECM markets are structurally mispriced due to a lack of engaged fundamental investors willing to underwrite deals, provide quality feedback, and hold positions beyond the first day of trading. strategy.sub_strategy: Directional equity long/short with net long bias
strategy.description: ALTO is a directional fundamental long/short equity fund focused on 300+ liquid, quality stocks in Europe and North America on the long side and a broader universe on the short side. The portfolio runs with an approximately 80–100% net long bias, diversified across 30–40 core long positions (sized 5–14% of NAV) and 40–50 single-stock shorts (sized 2–5% of NAV). The investment process is built on deeply-informed bottom-up stock analysis of a core monitored universe of 200–300 companies, targeting high-ROCE, high-gross-margin, structurally advantaged businesses with strong pricing power. Approximately half of ALTO's outperformance has historically come from stock selection and half from portfolio construction and dynamic sizing. The fund avoids companies overly dependent on macro or over-hyped themes, and uses index shorts (Eurostoxx 600, S&P 500) as part of the short book.
strategy.investment_thesis_core: Exploits systematic undervaluation of high-quality compounders (high ROCE, strong pricing power, low leverage) that are periodically derated by short-term market participants, combined with shorting structurally challenged or overvalued businesses to generate alpha on both sides of the book.
strategy.idea_generation: Closely monitors a core universe of 200–300 companies across Europe and North America. Ideas enter the portfolio via two routes: companies performing exceptionally well or those suffering a setback creating an attractive entry point. Approximately 40 research papers written per year; bi-weekly team meetings to discuss new ideas and core names. Proprietary quantitative infrastructure built by in-house CTO used to track relative valuations and pair relationships between similar businesses.

strategy.description: Arc24 is a New York-based credit-focused investment firm targeting double-digit returns by investing in the residential housing ecosystem and asset-backed securities. The strategy employs fundamental relative value through rigorous bottom-up analysis across three core strategies: Residential Mortgage-Backed Securities (RMBS, including Legacy, CRT, and Non-QM/RTL), Asset-Backed Securities (ABS, primarily Aviation ABS), and Mortgage Credit (REIT debt, preferred stock, and to a small extent common stock). strategy.investment_thesis_core: Exploits asymmetric risk-return opportunities in distressed and mispriced structured credit—particularly Aviation ABS (COVID-impacted, trading at GFC-like discounts) and residential housing credit—where proprietary Arconomics analytics identify superior risk-adjusted returns unavailable to generalist investors lacking deep domain expertise.

strategy.sub_strategy: Specialist structured and corporate credit
strategy.description: ASCIL invests in structured and corporate credit markets across Europe and the US, targeting bonds mispriced from a risk-reward perspective with limited correlation to overall credit markets. The fund employs four investment strategies: (1) Catalyst Driven Credit — investments with solid credit fundamentals and an identifiable value catalyst that unlocks convex returns; (2) Tactical Credit — bifurcation of credit versus fundamentals, market dislocations, and opportunistic participation in new issues; (3) Direct Origination — high-quality shorter-term lending directly sourced by Astra with alpha gained through sourcing and proprietary securitisation; and (4) Short Opportunities — fundamental short views via credit default swaps or as capital structure relative value. The fund invests across CLOs, RMBS, CMBS, CDOs, corporate bonds, CDS, and sovereign instruments, with a strong European tilt (typically 79–93% Europe).
strategy.investment_thesis_core: Exploits persistent pricing inefficiencies in structured credit arising from regulatory-driven imbalances, complexity premia, and rating migration dislocations. The team leverages its proprietary database and Deutsche Bank-era expertise to source bespoke cash and synthetic ABS portfolios that are mispriced relative to their underlying collateral quality, generating uncorrelated returns by isolating single-bond mispricings while largely avoiding broader market risks.
strategy.idea_generation: Macro-economic overlay combined with regulatory environment and demand-supply technicals determines investment theme; team then selects appropriate credit sub-asset class and geography. Sources include secondary market BWICs, primary issuance, direct origination from borrowers, and proprietary CLO/CMBS/RMBS database tracking hundreds of bonds and thousands of loans. Investment committee evaluates each opportunity through stepwise process: market analysis, asset sourcing, structural analysis, collateral analysis, relative value, asset strategy, risk analysis, and exit strategy.
strategy.family_defining_note: The fund is a specialist credit strategy focused on structured products (CLOs, RMBS, CMBS, CDOs) and corporate credit, with active short book via CDS. It is not a traditional long/short equity or macro fund.

strategy.sub_strategy: Systematic volatility relative value with long convexity bias in U.S. single-name equity options
strategy.description: Attimet runs a systematic U.S. equity options strategy focused on capturing idiosyncratic volatility opportunities across liquid single-name and index options. The strategy is long single-name options (primarily near-dated, near-the-money) across approximately 500 liquid U.S.-listed equities and ADRs, selectively offset with short index option positions (primarily SPY) to hedge macro/market-wide volatility exposure and reduce theta bleed. The portfolio is actively delta-hedged at both single-name and index levels. Return drivers are idiosyncratic vol mispricing across the single-name complex; the strategy does not short single-name options. Portfolio construction incorporates quantitative volatility forecasting, cross-name correlation modeling, sector/factor exposure balance, and execution-aware sizing. The universe is planned to expand to 2,000 underlyings. Turnover is very high with positions rarely held more than 8 days.
strategy.investment_thesis_core: U.S. single-name options markets contain persistent structural inefficiencies driven by fragmented liquidity, dealer inventory constraints, covered-call selling flows, and price-insensitive end-user demand, causing implied volatility to systematically diverge from expected realized volatility in ways that large market makers cannot fully arbitrage due to risk limits and existing inventory.
strategy.idea_generation: Quantitative volatility forecasting models trained on market data (stock and options) and alternative structured data (dividends, earnings events); AI agents scan unstructured data for fundamental/news/business changes affecting underlying uncertainty. System forecasts realized vol at expiry across the vol term structure; positions initiated when implied vol diverges from model forecast. Approximately 60% systematic, 40% discretionary overlay currently, with ambition to reach 80–90% systematic.

strategy.description: Fundamental long/short equity strategy primarily focused on the financial services sector, employing a broad active coverage model that follows both holdings and non-holdings with equal tenacity across ~150 actively covered names from a universe of ~466 companies. The strategy generates alpha on both the long and short side through bottom-up stock selection, with emphasis on single-name alpha shorts rather than index hedges. The portfolio typically holds 30-40 longs and 35-45 shorts with gross exposure of 150-250% and net exposure of 0-30% (averaging ~20%). Geographic focus is primarily U.S. with small allocations to developed Europe and Asia.
strategy.investment_thesis_core: Exploits the complexity, cyclicality, and regulatory specificity of financial services companies, which creates persistent equity market mispricing. Deep sector expertise and broad coverage of all financial subsectors—including banks, asset managers, brokers, FinTech, insurance, real estate, and specialty finance—allows early identification of inflection points and the ability to take full-size positions immediately. Short alpha from identifying 'fake FinTechs' and balance-sheet-mismanaged banks has contributed over 50% of ITD total portfolio return.
strategy.idea_generation: Bottom-up research using a systematic 13-week cycle: post-earnings outreach (weeks 0-2), formal company communication via standardized calls (weeks 2-6), buy-side and sell-side crosscheck (weeks 7-8), intensive modeling and earnings prep (weeks 9-10), and processing earnings reports (weeks 11-13). Ideas ranked on quantitative risk/reward skew, market sentiment, company history, short interest, and liquidity. CIO makes final investment and sizing decisions. Ongoing diligence includes macroeconomic data, master trust credit, asset manager flows, exchange trading volumes, and FED H8 loan data.

strategy.description: Fundamental discretionary long/short equity strategy investing in equities of companies primarily located in Continental Europe, with particular geographic focus on Switzerland, Germany and the Nordics. A majority of investments are in smaller market capitalizations and emerging growth companies. The fund seeks to identify companies across sectors where growth is accelerating and valuations are improving. risk_framework.risk_framework_description: Disciplined rule-based risk management at both position and portfolio level. Position-level: long investment requires >3:1 risk/reward; short requires >30% downside within 6 months. Risk trigger 1: position down -10% is cut in half unless good reason. Risk trigger 2: position down -20% targets liquidation. Profit taking when position exceeds 5% NAV (cut back to 3%). Portfolio-level: equiweight core positions at max 3% at cost (shorts max 2%); max sector risk 30% at cost; worst position liquidated every quarter. Market exposure target beta 0 to 0.7x market. Liquidity monitored daily with goal of exiting positions within 10 days under normal conditions. Hedge book uses proprietary market cycle model (RoboBen/macro leading indicators, risk asset trend model, asset valuation, contrarian indicators) to set net exposure target: bullish 0.5-0.7, sideways 0.2-0.5, bearish 0-0.2.
risk_framework.drawdown_response_protocol: Position-level risk triggers force selling: -10% triggers cut in half; -20% triggers target liquidation. Portfolio-level: in severe drawdowns (as demonstrated in Q1 2020), beta target reduced to lowest range (<0.3), gross exposure cut to ~50%, hedges added via put spreads. Risk management discipline forces reduction of risk in short period.

risk_framework.sector_limits: Max 30% risk per sector at cost
risk_framework.stop_loss_policy: Position down -10%: cut in half unless good reason. Position down -20%: target liquidation.

strategy.description: Aurora is a healthcare-dedicated long/short equity strategy operating as a team within Brummer & Partners, led by PM Hans Mähler. The strategy invests across four sub-sectors: Pharma/Biotech (~40% of GMV, predominantly US), Healthcare Equipment & Services (~30–35%, predominantly European/Nordic), Life Sciences Tools, and Consumer Health (smallest). The investment universe covers ~800 listed healthcare companies in the US and Europe with market cap above EUR 500m, of which the team has deep insight into ~150. The strategy is research-driven and event/catalyst-oriented: biotech positions are driven by clinical data readouts and approvals, while med tech positions are driven by earnings revisions and expectations mismatches. The team uses a concentrated long book (~30 names, 2–12% NAV each) and a short book (~35 names, 2–8% NAV each). The strategy targets market neutrality (dollar neutral and neutral to 5 selected factor betas). Gross exposure runs at approximately 130–225% (realised LTM 150–170%). The team deliberately avoids managed care and hospitals.
strategy.investment_thesis_core: Edge is sourced from deep, long-standing sector expertise (especially Nordic/European med tech and biotech), a science advisory network with unique access to protein and DNA sequencing experts, and the ability to trade fast around catalysts and US biotech pre-market news. The team exploits clinical data interpretation skills to identify longs with asymmetric upside at data readouts and shorts that are scientifically impressive but commercially unviable.
strategy.idea_generation: Approximately 800 companies divided across analyst and advisor coverage. Joseph Bergenstråhle covers pharma/biotech (sweet spot $1–10bn market cap, late-clinical to early-commercial, event/catalyst-driven with 6–12 month catalyst horizon). Carl Mellerby covers med tech (numbers-driven, detailed models, earnings revision turns, primary filings analysis). Advisory board members Frederik Dahl (DNA/tools) and Simon Fredriksson (proteins) provide scientific input on ~10–30 names in the tools space. Weekly 1-hour team meeting plus ad hoc discussion. PM reviews all ideas and makes final sizing/timing decisions.

market_views.macro_thesis: Markets are increasingly short-sighted, momentum/flow-driven, and dominated by passive money and pod structures, causing capital to move in the same direction and creating crowding risks. Rotations and flows can cause large, underestimated pain distinct from factor risk. The team focuses on staying factor-neutral to minimise this. Oncology is undergoing a paradigm shift with intense financing activity; liquid biopsies are a key area of traction. Med tech valuations have de-rated sharply.
sector_views: Oncology: paradigm shift underway; liquid biopsies a key area of traction and intense financing; team expects a basket of winners rather than a single winner.

Med tech: valuations have de-rated sharply (e.g. Coloplast trading at ~13x earnings); European med tech has been a strong alpha source; team wants to increase gross exposure to med tech given stable, low-volatility returns.

Biotech: event/catalyst-driven; standard of care improvements are making some gene-editing and gene-therapy approaches commercially unviable despite scientific impressiveness (e.g. Intellia, haemophilia gene therapy).
Medical packaging: double-digit growth area benefiting from GLP-1 capacity expansion.
Hearing aids: long/short pairs among five majors (Sonova, Demant, WS Audiology, GN, Starkey) plus Amplifon; playing trends (analogue to digital, smartphone connectivity, rechargeable, AI).
Life sciences tools: Illumina facing competitive threat from Roche's new sequencing system; sequencing becoming a shelf product.
geographic_views: Nordic/European med tech: outstanding alpha source; team has strong network and relationships with founders and owners.
US biotech: majority of biotech book; high liquidity enabling larger positions.
No US med tech exposure (deliberately removed after poor early performance; European med tech has been positive almost every month since the change).
key_risks_identified: Short-squeeze risk in biotech names and US retail-driven names (e.g. Moderna, CRISPR).

Regulatory/reimbursement risk in managed care and hospitals (deliberately avoided).
Middle East tensions cited as a factor in near-term market behaviour.
market_views.forward_outlook: Team plans to sign one external SMA in 2026. Ambition to grow to $1bn AUM while maintaining performance. Med tech book expected to continue generating stable, low-volatility returns. Biotech book expected to continue generating higher absolute returns with higher volatility. Team believes they can deliver the same numbers at $1bn.

strategy.description: Callodine Capital Fund targets the dividend-paying equity universe, investing in cash-generative mid-to-large cap U.S. companies across diverse industries including specialty income niches (BDCs, MLPs, REITs). The strategy combines a proprietary quantitative screening model (universe of ~1,200 stocks) with deep fundamental balance-sheet-driven research. Longs target high-quality, growing companies with strong free cash flow to enterprise value and dividend growth potential; shorts target companies with stressed balance sheets, deteriorating fundamentals, and potential dividend cuts (Dividend Cut Anticipation Model). Portfolio is constructed in three macro buckets (GDP-levered cyclicals, non-GDP-levered defensives, markets/rates/credit-levered financials) with net exposure managed within each bucket to avoid net-short positions in any single bucket. Typical portfolio: 20-30 longs, 30-40 shorts, 25-50% net exposure, 150-190% gross exposure.
strategy.investment_thesis_core: Exploits behavioral and valuation inefficiencies specific to dividend-paying equities, which have disproportionate retail ownership and are under-covered by institutional investors, creating predictable pricing dynamics. The strategy generates returns through a combination of portfolio yield (5%+ net), stock-selection alpha on both long and short sides, and low market beta.
strategy.idea_generation: Proprietary quantitative model screens ~1,200-stock equity income universe for upside/downside skew and preliminary price targets. Identifies 100-150 high-potential long and short candidates. Analysts perform balance-sheet-driven deep-dive fundamental research (3-statement analysis), verifying growth drivers and capital allocation trends. Investment team discussion precedes position sizing. Short ideas sourced via Dividend Cut Anticipation Model identifying companies with stressed balance sheets and unsustainably high dividend payout ratios.
strategy.market_cap_focus: small to mega cap
strategy.family_defining_note: The strategy is anchored in the dividend-paying equity income universe with a value tilt; the three-bucket macro construction framework is a defining structural feature introduced after the 2020 drawdown.

risk_framework.risk_framework_description: CIO James Morrow monitors portfolio long, short, net, gross, sector and sub-sector exposure on a real-time basis via Enfusion OMS (pre-trade compliance) and Barra/MSFS factor analytics. Portfolio is structured in three macro buckets (GDP-levered cyclicals, non-GDP-levered defensives, markets/rates/credit-levered financials); the firm does not allow net-short positions in any single bucket. Hard limits per the Lighthouse IAA Schedule B: gross exposure ≤225% NRA, net exposure ≤±55% NRA, max long position ≤10% NRA, max short position ≤5% NRA, top-5 issuer net exposure ≤50% NRA, minimum 20 longs and 25 shorts, sector gross ≤75% NRA, sector net ≤±20% NRA. Liquidity limits: ≤5% gross in securities >1x ADV, 0% in securities >2x ADV.
risk_framework.drawdown_response_protocol: No pre-set stop-loss rules. Positions are monitored on an ongoing basis; when a position moves significantly, the investment team re-underwrites the name and exits if the thesis is proven wrong. The 2020 drawdown led to a structural change: the portfolio now maintains three balanced macro buckets and does not go net-short in any bucket, which reduced volatility from mid-teens to 9-10%.

strategy.description: The Credit Opportunities Fund is an opportunistic, high-conviction, idiosyncratic best-ideas portfolio targeting 8–12% p.a. net returns over the credit cycle. The fund invests across European sub-investment grade credit including high yield bonds, leveraged loans, CLOs (mezzanine and equity), ABS, financial bonds, and equity-type instruments. The investment universe spans European and US credit markets with a focus on dislocations and relative value across the capital structure. All investments are decided unanimously by the security selection committee. The portfolio typically holds 50–80 positions with a maximum 20% concentration per single issuer for securities of the same type.
strategy.investment_thesis_core: Exploits market inefficiencies and dislocations across European sub-investment grade credit by applying fundamental bottom-up credit research and selection, with a focus on idiosyncratic opportunities across bonds, loans, CLOs, and structured credit that are mispriced relative to their recovery potential.

Ideas sourced from Capital Four's scaled credit platform of 20+ analysts covering all sectors. Unanimous decision-making by portfolio managers provides a high hurdle rate. Capital markets function manages primary pipeline and secondary opportunities.

strategy.sub_strategy: Systematic market-neutral US equity liquidity arbitrage
strategy.description: Systematic, market-neutral US equity strategy with two complementary components: (1) liquidity provision, which captures price reversion after large flow-driven dislocations, and (2) liquidity anticipation, which builds inventory ahead of expected demand, generating P&L during stress and providing defensive ballast. The model estimates abnormal supply/demand pressure across approximately 1,000 large/megacap US equities (mostly Russell 1000). Positions are sized through a proprietary company clustering technique derived from fundamental business models rather than statistical methods, grouping stocks by common business drivers to neutralize idiosyncratic business risk. Portfolio construction dynamically hedges residual factor risks so that P&L is driven predominantly by idiosyncratic alpha (75%+ idiosyncratic contribution to risk). The strategy rebalances twice daily with holding periods ranging from days to months; annual turnover exceeds 175x SAV. Leverage runs approximately 5.1x live. The two components are approximately -0.4 correlated (based on backtest), providing a natural hedge during stress periods.
strategy.investment_thesis_core: Exploits systematic supply/demand imbalances in large/megacap US equities caused by buy-side trading flows; the PM's 18 years of identifying and quantifying buy-side trading impact is formalized into a systematic framework that monetizes liquidity premia by providing liquidity after dislocations and anticipating future demand.
strategy.idea_generation: Proprietary clustering of ~150–185 Russell 1000 stocks into fundamental business-model groups (2–15 stocks each); within each cluster, a simulated supply/demand metric identifies abnormal flow pressure. Clusters are constructed bottom-up using fundamental analysis (~80% of the process) validated by a quantitative data model. The model uses structured and unstructured data including fine-grain trading data, implied curves, and aggregated tick data. No training on returns; parameters are fixed and parsimonious (1–2 parameters).

strategy.sub_strategy: Global multifactor quantitative equity market neutral, Ex-US focus
strategy.description: Quantitative global equity market neutral strategy targeting stock mispricing in ex-US developed markets, with a focus on small- and mid-cap stocks (minimum $500M market cap, equal-weight construction) where mispricing is most pronounced. Uses gradient boosting and neural network machine learning models trained on a rolling 15-year window to combine 40+ factors (approximately 50% fundamental, 50% technical) across categories including momentum, value, profitability, stability, sentiment, and long-term reversal. Signals are scored and combined into a multi-factor aggregate ranking for approximately 4,000 ex-US stocks; proprietary optimization creates a market neutral (zero beta) portfolio with sector, currency, and country neutrality constraints. Portfolio rebalances quarterly on a staggered basis with a 3-month forecast/hold period. Over 50% of model variables are proprietary or transformed. SHAP decompositions are used to interpret variable importance and interactions. Long-term reversal variables were added in 2023 to mitigate momentum crash risk; factor momentum variables added in 2025.
strategy.investment_thesis_core: Exploits systematic mispricing in ex-US small- and mid-cap equities where analyst coverage is low and anomaly returns are most pronounced, using machine learning models that identify nonlinear factor interactions and dynamic factor timing that linear regression models cannot capture. Competitive advantage is the application of cutting-edge ML (gradient boosting, neural networks) in the SMID-cap ex-US space, a segment too small for large quant managers like AQR.
strategy.idea_generation: Proprietary ML platform scores 40+ factors for approximately 4,000 ex-US developed market stocks daily. Factors sourced from S&P Global, Bloomberg, Markit. Multiple grading models weighted by predictive power produce an aggregate score per name, corrected for short borrow costs. SHAP decompositions identify variable importance and interactions. Model retrained on rolling 15-year window. Variables tested for efficacy since 2000 before inclusion.

strategy.description: Fully systematic multi-strategy portfolio harvesting a large variety of statistical anomalies in US equities, equity ETFs, and index futures. The engine combines approximately 530 alpha models in library (currently ~20 deployed), split between a Mean Reversion Cluster (~80% allocation, short-horizon dislocations around volatility/flow shocks and factor reversals across 1–30 day horizons) and a Momentum Cluster (~20% allocation, transitional momentum regime capture over 1–8 weeks). Signal generation uses a hybrid AI architecture combining domain-informed priors with machine-learning and genetic-algorithm engines that autonomously evolve signal formulas. Portfolio construction uses sigma-scaled discrete signal-tier sizing, a geometric kappa exposure overlay (25–100%), and hard beta, volatility, and factor caps. strategy.description: Fully systematic, market-neutral U.S. equity long/short strategy that seeks to exploit subtle, second-order, nonlinear relationships in market data using proprietary AI and machine learning techniques. The strategy has no economic priors or fundamental analysis; instead it uses a proprietary 'alpha blender' framework to generate, evaluate, and blend thousands of predictive signals derived from technical data, options pricing, and vendor data. The portfolio is constructed to be dollar and beta neutral, with dynamic leverage ranging from 2x to 6x depending on the system's confidence in its predictions. The strategy trades once daily near the market close and holds positions for days to weeks. The universe consists of 2,000–3,000 of the most liquid U.S. equity names, with a typical portfolio of 1,000–3,000 positions. Geographic exposure is 85–90% U.S. with most of the balance in Europe.
strategy.investment_thesis_core: Alpha is generated through proprietary machine learning primitives and a 'no priors' empirical approach that allows algorithms to find predictive patterns in technical and options pricing data. The edge lies in algorithm design rather than data acquisition—specifically the proprietary alpha blender framework that prevents predictive collapse and enables diversification across thousands of signals.
strategy.idea_generation: Signals ('experts') are generated using proprietary ML techniques trained on technical data, options pricing, and vendor data. New alphas are constructed by training ML models on features derived from market data. Models undergo out-of-sample validation. The alpha blender merges signals into a cohesive portfolio, penalizing correlated signals. New signals can be deployed in as little as one week. Most signals have zero weight on any given day; only a minority contribute meaningfully to the portfolio.

strategy.description: FordWellington runs a systematic, completely market-neutral long/short equity strategy applied to liquid large-cap US equities (S&P 500 + Nasdaq 100, approximately 550 names), with international variants covering Europe, Japan, Hong Kong, Brazil, and India. The alpha engine ingests approximately 500 Bloomberg data items per company (fundamental, market, analyst estimates, calculated/derived, sentiment) and assigns fixed binary coefficients (+1 or -1) based on first-principles discounted cash flow logic. Items are cross-sectionally ranked and aggregated through an ensemble of 75+ sub-models across daily, weekly, and monthly cadences, dynamically combined. The output is a Predicted Market Cap Rank; the difference between actual and predicted market cap rank constitutes alpha. Portfolios hold approximately 250 longs and 250 shorts with matched nominal values and beta. Portfolio construction uses a 3-layer optimizer in MATLAB minimizing downside variance and serial correlation. Average holding period is approximately 10-35 days. Hard-to-borrow names and announced M&A targets are excluded.
strategy.investment_thesis_core: Exploits systematic mispricings between actual market capitalizations and fundamental-valuation-implied market cap rankings using a first-principles DCF-derived scoring system with fixed binary coefficients that never adapt to recent data, producing idiosyncratic alpha uncorrelated to standard factor models and avoiding overfitting.
strategy.idea_generation: Bloomberg data ingested daily for approximately 500 items per company; items assigned fixed binary directionality coefficients based on monotonic, unambiguous impact on expected market valuation; cross-sectional pairwise comparisons aggregated through 75+ sub-models (including 2-3 neural network sub-models used as monitoring tools) across daily, weekly, and monthly cadences, dynamically combined in ensemble format; hard-to-borrow names and announced M&A targets excluded from universe.

risk_framework.risk_framework_description: Risk managed via hard exposure limits relative to Notional Risk Allocation (NRA) of $15 million. Gross exposure capped at 425% of NRA (typically ~400%). Net beta exposure limited to ±0.2% of NRA (measured as S&P 500 predicted beta, 1-day 1-year horizon). Net exposure limited to ±15% of NRA. Single long position max 5% of NRA; single short position max 5% of NRA (v3 limits). Top-5 issuer net exposures capped at 30% of NRA. Minimum 200 long and 200 short positions. Sector gross exposure capped at 65% of NRA; sector net exposure ±25% of NRA; net sector exposures limited to <5% of gross market value. Industry gross exposure capped at 35% of NRA; industry net exposure ±25% of NRA. Sub-$250m market cap gross exposure capped at 5% of NRA. Liquidity limits: max 5% gross in securities with >0.2x days' volume; 0% in securities with >1x days' volume. All hard-to-borrow and M&A stocks excluded. Portfolio construction uses a 3-layer optimizer in MATLAB minimizing covariance of returns plus adjusted/scaled prices and cumulative downside variance. Real-time monitoring of cross-correlations among names in the S&P 500 and Nasdaq universe versus exponential weighted averages over past 30 and 60 days provides early warning of unusual market environments. Over 80% idiosyncratic risk per Barra/Bloomberg factor models.
risk_framework.drawdown_response_protocol: If cross-correlation metric signals higher risk, optimizer targets lower risk level (adjusts relative weights to more diversified portfolio); second layer dynamically levers down, cutting all position sizes by up to 20-50%. Redeployment after de-risking is slower than the de-risking itself.

strategy.sub_strategy: UK mid-cap absolute return long/short equity
strategy.description: The fund employs a repeatable value-based process focused on UK mid-cap equities (market cap £100m–£10bn), investing at least 80% of assets in equities or financial derivative instruments relating to equities of UK-registered or UK-listed companies. The process classifies ideas into four types: Undervalued Assets (trading below tangible asset value or replacement cost), Undervalued Returns (cash-generative businesses trading below intrinsic value), Overvalued Value Traps (disappointing against expectations with poor cash generation and high leverage), and Overvalued Assets (inflated valuations relative to fundamentals). Long positions are held directly in equities; short positions are implemented synthetically via options. The fund targets an absolute return in excess of 3-Month Adjusted SONIA, running broadly market-neutral with gross exposure typically 120–150% and net exposure ranging from approximately -8% to +18%. The strategy has expanded into Nordic markets (Finland, Denmark, Norway, Sweden) since October 2024, representing approximately 16% of gross exposure as of April 2026.
strategy.investment_thesis_core: Exploits systematic mispricings in lesser-researched UK mid-cap equities by identifying companies whose tangible asset values or sustainable profit streams are materially mispriced relative to market price, using a static cost-of-capital framework focused on underlying cash generation, incremental returns, and scepticism of leverage. The proliferation of pod shops and passive investing has reduced career risk in markets, creating structural inefficiency the team aims to exploit by taking contrarian, concentrated positions.
strategy.idea_generation: Proprietary screen of UK mid-cap universe using EV/IC vs ROIC/WACC valuation matrix, classifying each company into one of four idea types. Long candidates require cash generation and positive operating momentum; short candidates require negative operating momentum, falling incremental returns, and growing debt. Management meetings are central to the process. The team covers approximately 150–200 companies deeply. Hit rates are tracked by sector. Flipping from long to short has a particularly high hit rate.

market_views.macro_thesis: AI is viewed as a structural disruptor likely to move profit pools over the next 10 years as significantly as the internet did, creating compelling short opportunities in companies that will lose relevance. The proliferation of pod shops, passives, and long-only funds means the proportion of market participants willing to take career risk is at historic lows, creating structural opportunity for differentiated active managers. Post-March 2026 dislocation viewed as creating Covid-like opportunities in cyclical international businesses. The team also identified a 'Hidden Volume Recession' thesis (2023–2024): a significant cumulative rise in nominal GDP since 2019 has masked volume declines in cyclical sectors, with corporate earnings expected to prove more resilient than consensus fears as volumes recover.

strategy.sub_strategy: Concentrated long/short value-biased equity
strategy.description: Concentrated long/short equity fund with a value bias investing primarily in US public equities with opportunistic global exposure. Employs deep fundamental bottom-up analysis to identify long and short alpha opportunities across consumer, media, telecom, industrials, technology, and other sectors. Portfolio generally consists of 30-50 longs and 10-30 shorts. Position sizing targets single-digit volatility with net exposure typically in the high 40% to low 50% range in recent years. Seeks companies with a clear 'path to outperformance' — inexpensive on FCF/EBITDA, management with strong capital allocation history, and identifiable catalysts. Shorts target companies with unsustainable earnings, aggressive accounting, or high short interest. AI and machine learning tools used as analytical aids for thesis validation and portfolio risk optimization.
strategy.investment_thesis_core: Exploits mispricing of undervalued companies with identifiable catalysts for earnings or multiple re-rating, using a proprietary 20+ year mosaic database and deep fundamental research to anticipate change before the market recognizes it, while maintaining a managed short book to reduce unintended market and industry exposures.
strategy.idea_generation: Proprietary screening database of 800+ names filtered to 10-20 best alpha-generating possibilities and 2-3 targets. Sources include company meetings and visits, industry conferences, financial publications, insider buying/selling analysis, short interest identification, and special situations (bankruptcies, spin-offs). Deep dive involves detailed financial models, management assessment, channel checks with former employees, competitors, suppliers, and customers.

strategy.sub_strategy: European equity event driven: 80% soft catalyst (pre-announced corporate events) and 20% hard catalyst (opportunistic merger arbitrage)
strategy.description: Gemian Capital Management runs a European event driven long/short equity strategy targeting 80% soft catalyst (pre-announced) and 20% hard catalyst (post-announced merger arbitrage) positions. Soft catalyst trades focus on mispriced corporate events including spin-offs, M&A, restructuring, litigation, and regulatory events predominantly in European equities. Hard catalyst positions are high-conviction merger arbitrage trades selected opportunistically on a global basis. The portfolio targets 30-50 alpha positions with leverage of 60-120% of capital, net exposure of +/-10%, and idiosyncratic risk >70%. All trades are scored on expected risk-adjusted return, liquidity, technicals, and portfolio diversification contribution via a proprietary scorecard. The strategy targets 10-12% net return on capital and a Sharpe ratio of 1.25-1.50, with 6-8% target volatility.
strategy.investment_thesis_core: European equity markets systematically misprice the probability and impact of corporate events (both possible and announced), creating exploitable alpha in soft catalyst positions where early positioning ahead of corporate activity generates returns uncorrelated to equity markets and other event driven strategies.
strategy.idea_generation: Proprietary screening of 5,000+ universe filtered to ~300 core tracked companies (tracked since 2011) and a 100-name watch list. Candidates scored on expected return, expected volatility (net of hedging costs), liquidity, technicals (price action and flow), and timing (proximity to catalyst). Weekly position-level reviews with P&L attribution, sizing adjustments, crowding/short interest checks, hedge effectiveness, and macro context.

strategy.description: Hudson Cove Credit Opportunity Fund seeks high absolute returns with low volatility and low correlation to broad equity and fixed income markets by investing in a hybrid of public securitized products (ABS/MBS) and privately negotiated asset-based lending (ABL) opportunities. The ABS/MBS book targets mispriced consumer and commercial finance structured credit products (auto, credit card, student loan, mortgage, equipment, timeshare) in primary and secondary markets. The ABL book focuses on $10-$40 million senior-secured facilities to US middle-market specialty finance companies, collateralized by cash-flowing receivables held in bankruptcy-remote SPVs, with conservative advance rates (60-90%), tight covenants, and performance triggers. The portfolio holds 80-150 positions with average duration under two years.
strategy.investment_thesis_core: Structural inefficiencies in ABS/MBS cause select bonds to trade wider than underlying collateral performance warrants; in private credit, regulatory constraints and bank focus on larger corporates create a gap for non-bank lenders like Hudson Cove to structure attractive ABL facilities at $10-$40 million deal sizes where competition is limited.
strategy.idea_generation: ABS/MBS: identified via broker/dealer relationships, new issuance, and secondary market; detailed credit analysis performed before presentation to CIO and Senior PM. ABL: sourced through proprietary network of specialty finance companies, dedicated brokers, boutique bankers, and institutional partners; onsite due diligence, background checks, third-party forensic accounting, and term sheet negotiation precede closing.

strategy.description: Discretionary, fundamentally driven Credit Relative Value strategy focused on generating alpha in all markets by identifying and exploiting mispriced credits in a low-net portfolio construct. The fund employs quantitative filters across a broad opportunity set to provide timely data-driven insights to support deep-dive fundamental analysis. The portfolio holds approximately 100 line items across 10 different sub-strategies including Credit Driven, Volatility, Event Driven, Tactical, Equity Like, and Structured. Approximately one-third of the book is shorts. Geographic split targets 20% US, 40% EMEA, 40% APAC over the cycle. Instruments include IG, HY, financials, convertible bonds, and equity-linked credit. The fund is active in new issuance and engages directly with syndicates, sponsors, and leveraged finance teams.
strategy.investment_thesis_core: Exploits mispriced optionality and structural inefficiencies in credit and convertible instruments — particularly embedded features such as make-whole payments, change-of-control adjustments, and incentivised conversion — that are systematically undervalued by conventional DCF and equity-volatility frameworks. Uses a 'corridor of confidence' framework to define the range of outcomes for each credit and identify catalysts for correction.
strategy.idea_generation: Proprietary quantitative screens price approximately 35,000 issuers daily to assess cheapness vs. historical context. Sub-strategy screens identify short-term tender trades, fundamental richness/cheapness by LTV and credit profile, and new issuance opportunities. Screens shortlist candidates for deep-dive fundamental underwriting by analysts. Team is wall-crossed on primary deals and engages directly with issuers, sponsors, and banking syndication teams.
strategy.neutrality_approach: low-net
strategy.family_defining_note: Credit Relative Value with convertibles, credit L/S, and macro overlays; approximately one-third of the book is shorts; geographic targets 20% US / 40% EMEA / 40% APAC over the cycle.

strategy.sub_strategy: Asia-Pacific fundamental long/short equity
strategy.description: Keyrock deploys a research-intensive, fundamental long/short equity strategy focused primarily on small- and mid-cap companies in the Asia-Pacific region (market cap US$0.5bn–$20bn), with a primary focus on Japan and Korea. The investment process is non-consensus and idea-generation driven, combining local filings, on-the-ground investigations, management reference calls, and online data analytics. Long positions target companies that can double or more in 3 years (25%+ IRR hurdle); short positions target names with 25%+ downside in 1 year. The portfolio runs 5–15 longs and 15–35+ shorts under 'Keyrock 2.0' portfolio construction, with core long positions sized at ~15% NAV and core shorts at ~6% NAV. The fund also makes selective private investments in pre-IPO Japanese companies as a natural extension of its public equity research.
strategy.investment_thesis_core: Exploits information asymmetry in under-covered Asia-Pacific growth companies—particularly Japanese and Korean equities—where limited sell-side coverage, early-stage public listings, and structural digital transformation tailwinds create mispriced opportunities. The edge is deep on-the-ground primary research including 20+ management reference calls per investment and proprietary channel checks.
strategy.idea_generation: Non-consensus approach combining local filings, on-the-ground investigations, management reference calls (20+ per investment), industry expert networks, and online data analytics. Ideas sourced from corporate actions, sector digitization themes, and regulatory change catalysts. Private company research supplements public equity pipeline by providing early access to pre-IPO businesses.

strategy.description: KL Special Opportunities Fund is a concentrated portfolio of predominantly hard-catalyst, near-term investments designed to extract returns from opportunities across the capital structure. The fund operates four sub-strategies: global merger arbitrage (core, typically 50–80% of gross assets), equity event, Euro-centric credit opportunities, and distressed. risk_framework.risk_framework_description: Positions hedged individually with cost of hedging reflected in return expectations. Residual market sensitivity aggregated into beta-adjusted net exposure metric. Portfolio hedge implemented via S&P 500 and Eurostoxx 50 option strategies and futures to keep beta-adjusted net exposure after hedge between -10% and +20% of NAV (in practice targeting near 0%). Individual position worst-case loss tolerance of 1.5% of NAV. Stress test conducted assuming concurrent 20% equity market drop, two riskiest M&A positions breaking, and M&A spreads widening 3% across the board. Risk Committee oversight with override authority. strategy.description: Absolute return, fundamental bottom-up long/short equity strategy focused primarily on ASX300 companies (minimum 70% of gross exposure in Australia), with up to 30% of gross exposure in international developed markets (US, Canada, Europe, Hong Kong). The strategy combines DCF-based valuation (50% of stock ranking) with qualitative scoring across management quality, industry structure, and business trends (50% of ranking). strategy.sub_strategy: European stressed credit long/short event-driven
strategy.description: Fundamental, bottom-up, value-based approach targeting mispriced stressed credit in the segment between performing and distressed European credit. The strategy invests long in approximately 20 high-conviction positions in corporate bonds, convertible bonds, syndicated loans and CDS where risk is mispriced due to situation-specific complexity (misunderstood business models, balance sheet issues, jurisdictional intricacy). Alpha shorts target junior credit instruments in senior-friendly jurisdictions with a clear path to zero recovery in a senior-led restructuring, often paired with a long senior leg for neutral carry. Residual market exposure is managed via TRS on the iBoxx liquid HY index. Geographic focus is Northern/Western Europe (UK, Benelux, Scandinavia, Germany, France, Switzerland). Average holding period of approximately two years; portfolio turns over approximately one new investment per one to two months. Capacity stated at $1.5bn.
strategy.investment_thesis_core: Institutional reluctance to underwrite situation-specific complexity in European stressed credit causes price-indiscriminate selling around rating downgrades, bad results and corporate events, enabling a fundamental investor to earn ~15% net returns on a risk profile consistent with ~5% return in the performing segment.
strategy.idea_generation: Screening of ~2,000 European credit names via on-market and off-market proprietary network channels; filtered to ~200-name watchlist via pricing screen, then ~60-name pipeline via fundamental valuation screen including ESG filter; approximately one new investment selected every one to two months based on risk/reward optimisation.
strategy.neutrality_approach: Beta neutral / market neutral

risk_framework.risk_framework_description: Three-level risk management framework covering position, portfolio and firm levels. Position level: margin of safety as foundation for all decisions; soft stop-loss triggering full re-underwriting and possible exit; liquidity caps (max % of tranche owned, minimum broker quotes); constant monitoring of credit deterioration and factor risks. Portfolio level: maximum position size 15% of NAV (most positions 5-10%); maximum net sector exposure <25% of NAV; credit market widening hedged via single-name shorts and index TRS; interest rate risk managed via duration/convexity analysis and hedges; ongoing liquidity monitoring vs fund terms. Firm level: full compliance processes, independent valuation/administration, business continuity procedures, counterparty due diligence.
risk_framework.drawdown_response_protocol: Soft stop-loss at position level triggers full re-underwriting review and possible exit. Portfolio is deliberately positioned with low/neutral market exposure so that the Fund can be a buyer at times of market dislocation rather than a forced seller.
risk_framework.position_limits: Max 15% of NAV per long position; most positions 5-10% of NAV. Max 15% of NAV per short position. IAA limits: max long position 15% NRA, max short position 15% NRA, max expected loss per position 3.5% NRA.
risk_framework.sector_limits: Target net maximum sector exposure <25% of NAV; max long exposure to single sector 25% NRA; max gross exposure to single sector 40% NRA (per IAA).
risk_framework.stop_loss_policy: Soft stop-loss at position level triggering full underwriting review and possible exit.

strategy.description: Fundamental equity long/short strategy focused exclusively on European issuers. The long book invests in durable assets with sustainable earnings power, assessed through five dimensions: Management, Return on Capital, Sustainability of Returns, Ability to Deploy Incremental Capital at High Return, and Earnings Quality. The short book is an independent profit centre combining forensic accounting with fundamental research, using proprietary databases, accounting screens, and targeted textual searches. Long book targets 20-30 positions sized at 2%, 4%, or 8% of NAV; short book targets 30-40 positions sized at 1%, 2%, or 4% of NAV. Target exposures are 150% gross and 50% net. strategy.description: Fundamental long/short equity strategy focused on technologically driven disruption in tech and adjacent sectors globally (including consumer, healthcare services, and industrials). Concentrated portfolio of 40–50 liquid absolute return longs and shorts with limited hedges. Net exposure typically 30–70% driven bottom-up by idea generation. Longs held 3–5 years targeting dominant platforms, business model transitions ('Tweeners'), and digitisation opportunities ('Future #1s'); shorts held 1–2 years targeting misunderstood IPOs/SPACs, disrupted companies, and quality traps. Investment team is also the data team, purchasing raw alternative datasets (email receipts, cloud spend, POS data) to generate differentiated insights. Universe is companies >$2bn market cap; shorts typically $2–10bn. Objective is to capture 1x market return in up-markets and 0.5x or less in down-markets.
strategy.investment_thesis_core: Exploits market inefficiencies in an expanding tech universe by vertically integrating fundamental research with creative use of raw alternative data, enabling differentiated mid-term earnings estimates particularly in adjacent sectors (healthcare services, consumer, industrials) where tech's impact is misunderstood, and in smaller-cap shorts ($2–10bn) where competition is limited.
strategy.idea_generation: Search for change in companies, industries, and own behaviour. Sources: corporate action announcements, IPOs/SPACs, industry digitisation trends, alternative data signals. Two-stage research process: 2-day initial thesis (hypothesis, simple model, risk/reward framing) followed by 2-month full research (detailed financial model, custom alternative data, primary research including management meetings, expert networks, surveys, unit economics analysis). Evidence Tracker monitors thesis KPIs.

strategy.description: Market-neutral, rules-based long/short stock-picking strategy focused on approximately 1,500 European listed stocks in the €3–15bn market cap range (~70–80% Eurozone, ~20–30% Sweden). The stated alpha source is structured analysis of underutilised corporate disclosures, regulatory filings, and legal frameworks, combined with analyst estimate data, short interest, crowding signals, price/volume action, and credit market context. The process flows through four stages: systematic screening (signal capture), binary risk/reward diligence, risk/liquidity-driven position sizing (no conviction trades), and daily re-underwriting with 17 potential exit criteria. The portfolio targets ~200 positions (80–100 per leg), equal-weighted at 0.25–0.5% average with 1% max for longs and <0.8% max for shorts. Gross exposure runs at 180–200% (unlevered); net exposure managed at 0 to ±10%. The long book is live as Fundamental Select UCITS (launched November 2024); the short book has been tracked and logged daily with Lighthouse as a named third party since 12 November 2024 but has never traded live.
strategy.investment_thesis_core: Exploits information asymmetries in underutilised European corporate filings and legal frameworks — data systematically overlooked by mainstream analysts — to identify operational trajectories before they are broadly priced in, generating idiosyncratic alpha on both long and short sides independently of market direction.
strategy.idea_generation: Proprietary four-stage process: (1) automated signal capture via data scraping and binary classification of corporate filings, regulatory disclosures, and legal frameworks across ~1,500 European names, filtering from tens of thousands of data points to ~2% after scrubbing; (2) Bayesian diligence combining quantitative and qualitative analysis with analyst estimates, short interest, crowding data, credit signals, and price/volume action; (3) risk/liquidity-driven sizing with no conviction bias; (4) daily re-underwriting with 17 defined exit criteria. Manual audits conducted every few weeks to verify system integrity.

risk_framework.risk_framework_description: Multi-layered risk controls at position, portfolio, and structural overlay levels. Position-level: daily bottom-up re-assessment based on beta, volatility, liquidity, correlations, and performance — breach equals exit. Portfolio-level: market neutrality enforced across currencies, countries, net/beta exposures, sectors and factors; 80–90% of book liquidatable in one day; ~80–100 positions per leg. Structural overlay: triggered only if both book volatility and market volatility breach predefined standard deviation limits. Own risk workbook in Excel uploaded into Bloomberg; Bloomberg VAR model used alongside proprietary factor model. Risk assessed daily; every position receives new risk limits every day. Axioma independently validates predicted beta of −0.01 and 79.7% residual/idiosyncratic risk as of 27 Feb 2026.
risk_framework.drawdown_response_protocol: If book is not optimal, reduce GMV. Cannot run the same GMV in all market environments; when there are larger bottom-up tilts, run less GMV. Adaptive stop-loss mechanism in place. Positions must justify their allocation every day; breach equals exit. At Bell Rock, sector exposure greater than 5% on each side triggered an index hedge.

strategy.description: Gravity is a 100% systematic, market-neutral, factor-neutral quantitative equity strategy focused on small- and mid-cap US-listed equities (75% of portfolio below $10bn market cap, minimum $150mn market cap, Russell 3000 universe), excluding biotech. The system applies advanced machine learning (gradient boosting trees, non-negative linear models, agglomerative clustering) to 3,000+ engineered fundamental features derived from SEC filings, CapIQ fundamentals, analyst estimates, and market data since 1996. Over 300–500 specialized ML models each act as a 'fundamental analyst,' predicting relative stock performance over a 1-month to 1-year horizon. A solver/optimizer layer dynamically weights model outputs and constructs a portfolio of approximately 800 longs and 800 shorts, neutralizing market, sector, size, value, momentum, and other risk-factor exposures. The portfolio targets 12% annualized gross volatility at 3x3 leverage (300% long, 300% short), with net market exposure near 0%. Median holding period is approximately 5 weeks; rebalancing occurs weekly on Mondays.
strategy.investment_thesis_core: Business fundamentals are the timeless long-term driver of stock performance and can be probabilistically predicted using ML; the market systematically misprices non-linear changes in business fundamentals in less-covered SMID-cap equities, creating exploitable alpha that is uncorrelated to macro, sector, and factor risks.
strategy.idea_generation: Automated ETL pipeline ingests SEC filings, CapIQ fundamentals, analyst estimates, and market data since 1996. Over 300–500 ML models trained on data through 2017 generate individual stock rankings. A solver/optimizer synthesizes model outputs, weights them by recent and long-term efficacy and inter-model correlation, and constructs a factor-neutral portfolio. Models are retrained and the target portfolio is regenerated weekly over the weekend; trades are placed Monday.
strategy.market_cap_focus: 75% below $10bn market cap; minimum $150mn market cap; Russell 3000 universe
strategy.neutrality_approach: Market neutral, sector neutral, factor neutral (value, momentum, size, quality, and other Barra/Axioma-style factors); net market, sector, and risk-factor exposure targeted at 0%
strategy.family_defining_note: Fully systematic; no discretionary trading. All risk limit breaches resolved by regenerating a compliant portfolio.

risk_framework.risk_framework_description: Risk is managed entirely within the portfolio construction optimizer, which neutralizes market, sector, size, value, momentum, and other Barra/Axioma-style factor exposures weekly. The system generates risk factors internally using calculations similar to BARRA and uses portfolio optimization software (cvxpy) to ensure roughly equal long and short exposure to each factor. Exposures are monitored in a real-time dashboard before and during the week. The portfolio is capped at <3% of any individual stock's daily trading volume. Leverage is maintained at 3x3 with a 2x margin of safety vs. worst simulated drawdown.
risk_framework.drawdown_response_protocol: No pre-set rule to cut exposure during drawdowns. Protocol: (1) maintain leverage cushion and not panic, (2) check for execution issues vs. simulation, (3) check for data issues, (4) re-review long-term strategy calibration, (5) investigate market environment. Leverage would only be reduced if VIX exceeded 40 (broker margin risk), cutting gross from 600% to 300%. The firm explicitly does not reduce exposure during normal drawdowns.

strategy.sub_strategy: Systematic long equity volatility
strategy.description: The One River Dynamic Convexity Strategy is a systematic long equity volatility strategy designed as a carry-efficient offset to equity market exposure. It combines three sub-strategies: (1) Dynamic Protection (60% weight) — a long-only VIX and VSTOXX futures CTA that modulates exposure based on the shape of the VIX term structure, increasing exposure as the curve inverts in stress and reducing as crisis subsides; (2) Always-On Protection (15% weight) — long VIX options (always long, never short) exploiting persistent dislocations on the volatility surface via VIX strangles/straddles that benefit from roll-down in benign markets and spike in crises; (3) Episodic Protection (25% weight) — equity index straddles on global indices with positive expected value as determined by a proprietary model scanning for mispriced options relative to upward drift and crash risk. The strategy never sells options to fund long volatility positions.
strategy.investment_thesis_core: Microstructure and behavioral phenomena create upside momentum in VIX futures; dislocations on the VIX volatility surface are large and persistent, exploitable systematically through option structures with fixed downside and unlimited upside; equity market options do not efficiently price the tendency for markets to drift higher or crash lower.
strategy.idea_generation: Systematic signals: VIX term structure shape determines exposure level and positioning on the curve for Dynamic Protection; VIX surface dislocation analysis (ETP flow-driven steep forwards vs. variance-swap-suppressed spot) drives Always-On Protection; proprietary decision tree combining technical indicators (moving averages, RSI, price extremity), asset-specific implied/realized volatility, and broad VIX regime determines Episodic Protection straddle deployment.
