strategy.sub_strategy: Behavioral sentiment-driven directional options strategy on S&P 500
strategy.description: The BASON Fund applies behavioral psychology and a proprietary crowd-survey model (BASON) to generate weekly directional signals for the S&P 500. The model aggregates sentiment from competitive crowd surveys of approximately 3,500 participants, using wisdom-of-crowds and network-theory techniques to eliminate groupthink and identify consistently accurate forecasters. The weekly signal is translated into rules-based positions via 2DTE and 0DTE SPY options (naked calls or puts), with a 2% maximum risk cap per week. From January 2026, the fund also runs a hedged long component (90% of portfolio in SPY/QQQ with put protection, based on a 90-day moving average of the BASON signal) alongside the core options strategy. The fund is fully systematic, uses no leverage, and does not short options naked.
strategy.investment_thesis_core: Markets are driven by sentiment that is socially formed and subject to groupthink; by identifying heterogeneous, consistently accurate forecasters through network analysis and competitive surveys, the fund can predict weekly S&P 500 direction with a stated 62% hit rate and generate uncorrelated, behaviorally-driven alpha.
strategy.idea_generation: Weekly competitive crowd surveys of ~3,500 participants; survey results received Wednesday mornings. Machine learning used to identify forecasters on 'hot streaks.' Signal output determines directional call or put position for the week. 2DTE options traded near Wednesday open (exit Friday before close); 0DTE options traded Thursday and Friday.

strategy.description: PAM's portfolio construction process is described as 'Catalyst-driven Relative Value,' focused on generating positive returns in all market regimes on an absolute basis. The investment approach identifies market dislocations where an asset's price may temporarily deviate from fair value due to non-fundamental reasons. Alpha is generated by distinguishing between fundamental impairments and non-fundamental dislocations with a discrete catalyst for reversion. Dislocations are bucketed as either Price (crowded trade unwinds, passive fund flows, index events, regulatory changes) or Structural (cross-border holdings, stub trade value unlock, shareholder activism targets). Proprietary tools aggregate structured and unstructured data to generate signals highlighting dislocated opportunities and facilitate hedging solutions. Primary focus is APAC liquid equities with tactical allocations to US/EU. Internal resource allocation targets: Japan 80%, HK/China/US ADRs 15%, Rest of Asia 5%. Portfolio instruments include equities long and short, convertible bonds, warrants, listed options, index futures, and OTC options. Portfolio turnover is approximately 10x per month for short-term strategies.
strategy.investment_thesis_core: Exploits temporary price dislocations in APAC liquid equities caused by non-fundamental factors including fund flow changes, multi-manager platform risk unwinds, quant strategy flows, cross-shareholding unwinds, and ECM/block transactions. Proprietary tools and deep relationships with Japanese domestic banks and sell-side ECM desks provide differentiated access to cross-shareholding unwind transactions at discounts, with a discrete catalyst and timeline for reversion.
strategy.idea_generation: Proprietary tools scan for correlation and breadth changes; intelligence gathered from sell-side ECM and trading desks; one-on-one meetings with investment bank corporates; tracking fund flows and positioning data from brokerages; monitoring Bloomberg holdings data for large shareholder changes; deep relationships with domestic Japanese banks for cross-shareholding unwind deal flow.

strategy.sub_strategy: Agency MBS derivatives relative value – prepayment risk premium capture (IO, IIO, PO)
strategy.description: Discretionary relative value strategy focused on structured Agency MBS, primarily Interest Only (IO), Inverse IO (IIO), and Principal Only (PO) securities, with smaller allocations to non-Agency RMBS credit (CRT, jumbo IO, HELOC residuals) and consumer ABS (student loan residuals). Portfolio A targets market-neutral returns by hedging interest rate, curve, and volatility exposures using Agency TBA contracts, Treasury futures, SOFR swaps, and swaptions. Security selection is driven by OAS models, proprietary prepayment models, and loan-level collateral analysis. The strategy exploits mispricing in Agency derivatives arising from prepayment risk complexity, with a particular focus on low-WAC, low-loan-balance collateral that provides prepayment protection.
strategy.investment_thesis_core: Agency IO and IIO securities are systematically mispriced because prepayment models are calibrated to prior refinancing waves (2003, 2021) that overstate future prepayment speeds given today's far-out-of-the-money borrower universe; this creates excess OAS that can be captured with disciplined hedging. IIO additionally offers an embedded yield-curve steepening option that is cheap relative to alternatives.

strategy.description: Savoir Faire Capital Management runs a low-net equity long/short strategy investing exclusively in US-listed liquid equities (including ETFs and ADRs/ADSs) with a core focus on consumer staples and discretionary sectors, plus select TMT and industrial names. The investable universe spans 300+ companies with market caps above $1B. The portfolio trades approximately 140–150 names organized into nine consumer sub-sectors (3 staples, 5 discretionary, 1 other), with roughly half to two-thirds of the book in paired trades (e.g., Coke vs. Pepsi, Home Depot vs. Lowe's) and the remainder in single-name positions. Staples positions are sized at 5–9% of NAV; discretionary positions at mid-to-low single digits. The portfolio runs at approximately 2x gross leverage (200% GMV) with net exposure typically 4–20% on GMV/NRA. Idea generation relies on proprietary primary research designed to avoid sell-side groupthink. A proprietary risk overlay (MATR) sizes positions, monitors correlations, and removes emotion from book construction. The book is rebalanced approximately monthly.
strategy.investment_thesis_core: Exploits fundamental mispricings between paired consumer staples and discretionary names using deep sector expertise built over 20+ years, with an edge in modeling slow-moving staples businesses underserved by sell-side research. The strategy generates idiosyncratic alpha (targeting 70%+ idio) by pairing names within sub-sectors to isolate specific business model differences, with low correlation to other equity L/S funds.
strategy.idea_generation: Primary research-driven: reads 10-Ks and 10-Qs, listens to management conference calls, analyzes Nielsen scanner data and consumer surveys, monitors consumer trends. Uses a proprietary T-account visualization system organized by 9 sub-sectors. Tracks hit rates and slugging ratios per position. Adds approximately 10 new names per year based on liquidity thresholds. Uses a quant (MIT professor, former BlueCrest colleague) who maintains a correlation matrix and tracks crowded shorts. Four-step process: Identify, Verify, Quantify, Document.

risk_framework.risk_framework_description: SFCM uses a proprietary risk system built around Moving Average Trading Ranges (MATR), which measures intra-stock and sector volatility not captured by traditional metrics, and serves as a position sizing and esoteric risk identification tool. Risk monitoring is organized into four areas: Positions (MATR-based sizing, short interest, borrow, catalysts, options-implied moves), Portfolio (correlations, pipeline, hit ratios by sub-sector), Environment (MATR of other sectors, commodity/currency/financing moves, sector cycle mapping), and Capital (drawdown-triggered capital reduction rules). Daily monitoring and weekly meetings are conducted. Axioma is used as a risk model (added recently). Tracks 30 different portfolio metrics. Uses a quant (MIT professor, former BlueCrest colleague) who maintains a correlation matrix and tracks crowded shorts.
risk_framework.drawdown_response_protocol: 0–1% DD: normal noise, no action. -1–2%: reposition MATR-flagged positions, increase hedges in at-risk sectors. -2–3%: individual names trigger reductions; cut 10% of capital for every 1% loss below 2%. -4–5%: risk metrics have reduced individual names and book-level rules have cut capital 30–40%; continue cutting aggressively and wait for investable environment after initial bounce; any further bleed met with aggressive capital reduction.
risk_framework.position_limits: Long: max 12% of NRA (contractual); Short: max 8% of NRA (contractual); top 5 issuers net exposure sum not to exceed 50% of NRA. Staples: 5–9% NAV; Discretionary: 1–4% NAV per operating practice.
risk_framework.sector_limits: Max gross exposure per GICS sector (other than Consumer Staples and Consumer Discretionary): 30% of NRA; max net exposure to single sector: ±20% of NRA. Geographic limits: US/Canada gross ≤315%, EU gross ≤15%, Asia gross ≤10%.
risk_framework.stop_loss_policy: Dollar stop losses on stock prices and P&L per position (e.g., $5M loss on a name); fundamental stop losses; stop losses set at cost. Portfolio-level: cut 10% of GMV for every 1% drawdown below 2%.

risk_framework.risk_framework_description: Risk managed at two layers. Single stock layer: update expected returns and maintain disciplined sizing; avoid confirmation bias and thesis drift; upon risk of thesis break, reduce or exit position and start fresh. strategy.description: Velox is a pan-European equity long-short market neutral strategy co-managed by Dimitri Kern and Jeremy Stone. The strategy systematically identifies repeatable patterns of investor behaviour around discrete events (earnings releases, rights issues, index rebalancings, management changes, M&A) using 1,500 proprietary systematic filters developed over 10+ years, organised into six investment themes: Results/Shock, Event Driven, Fundamental, Capital Markets, Technical Moves, and Arbitrage. Each PM trades an independent book; capital is dynamically allocated across the five strategies based on PM conviction and opportunity set. The investment universe is approximately 1,800 developed European stocks (>€200m market cap, >€500k ADV), filtered by an ESG exclusion list. The portfolio targets ~200 positions, 2/3 idiosyncratic risk and 1/3 factor risk, with gross exposure typically 140–185% and net exposure ±10%. ESG is integrated via a proprietary Traffic Light System and the ViA app, with the fund classified as SFDR Article 8.
strategy.investment_thesis_core: Markets are slow to fully incorporate new information; investors react predictably to similar events (earnings shocks, corporate actions, index events), creating repeatable, exploitable patterns of stock price behaviour that can be identified systematically and traded with disciplined risk management.
strategy.idea_generation: 1,500 systematic filters screen the ~1,800-stock European universe daily across six investment strategies. Signals are assessed through five lenses: Technical Analysis, Fundamental Analysis, Catalysts, Sentiment (street positioning), and ESG. PMs use the proprietary RAID/Trading Labs system for real-time screening, portfolio construction, and risk monitoring.

strategy.sub_strategy: Diversified systematic CTA — trend-following with diversifying signals
strategy.description: Winton's flagship CTA offering combines a core 75% trend-following allocation (hardwired at end-2020) with 25% diversifying signals (carry, mean-reversion, seasonality, fundamental models, futures market dynamics, cross-sector macro relationships) applied to more than 240 macro markets spanning major and alternative markets globally. Trend following blends multiple speeds of model to maximise risk-adjusted returns and portfolio diversification, incorporating features to counteract trend exhaustion via inverse volatility weighting and a non-linear response function. Position sizing is determined daily via a proprietary volatility forecasting model targeting approximately 10% annualised volatility; the portfolio is re-geared daily using correlation estimates and mean-variance optimisation. The strategy has no directional bias in equities and bonds.
strategy.investment_thesis_core: Profitable investment opportunities can be identified through advanced statistical and pattern-recognition techniques applied to large datasets; trend-following exploits systematic behavioural biases in market participants, while diversifying signals provide positive drift in non-trending environments. Diversification across uncorrelated markets transforms a faint per-market edge (Sharpe ~0.2) into a portfolio-level Sharpe of ~0.8.
strategy.idea_generation: Systematic daily portfolio construction: signal generation from multiple trend speeds and diversifying models → target positions via volatility-weighted mean-variance optimisation → pre-trade monitoring → order management → post-trade monitoring. Research projects prioritised by CIO based on return potential, feasibility and strategic alignment; material changes require Trading System Committee approval.
strategy.neutrality_approach: No long or short directional bias; seeks diversification across many uncorrelated markets
strategy.family_defining_note: Fully systematic, research-driven CTA with no discretionary overrides in normal market conditions; CIO retains discretion on leverage decisions in exceptional circumstances.

risk_framework.risk_framework_description: Multi-layered risk framework developed over 25+ years. Normal conditions monitoring: forecast volatility, realised volatility, betas to factors. Extreme conditions monitoring: net and gross leverage, margin-to-equity, historical stress test, volatility-based stress test, correlation-based stress test (including equity-bond correlation reversals as in March 2023 and May 2013 Taper Tantrum). Volatility estimates designed to be less sensitive to short-term changes; effect of diversification disappearing from portfolios monitored through time. Pre-trade: targeted volatility level (~10% annualised) set by Trading System Committee; sector/market weightings; speculative position limits enforced by exchanges/regulators; WCM system-level hard limits on max open position, max order size. Post-execution: proprietary Risk Manager system monitors margin-to-equity, notional-to-equity, VaR (1-day, 95% confidence), position/trading volumes vs. exchange open interest, position concentrations, and P&L daily. Independent Risk Management Function (second-line) reports to CCO. Counterparty risk monitored daily with excess balances swept to custody accounts.
risk_framework.drawdown_response_protocol: Risk management is designed in advance so that the strategy continues to trade as designed during large market moves without significant intervention. Leverage reduction decisions made by CIO on a consensus-driven basis, typically taking volatility to the lower end of the operating range. In exceptional market events (e.g. loss of liquidity, exchange closure), trading principals may exercise discretion to reduce gearing or liquidate positions in specific markets temporarily. Cutting risk during chaotic markets when liquidity is strained and transaction costs are elevated is considered the worst time to intervene.
risk_framework.position_limits: No more than 10% of NAV as initial margin in any single market; no more than 50% of NAV committed to clearing brokers as initial margin; max 7% of risk in any single market
risk_framework.sector_limits: Sector and market weightings set within models; soft limits monitored via Risk Manager; sector margin-to-equity monitored against soft limits
risk_framework.stop_loss_policy: No stop losses used in the main futures strategy; positions closed when trend reverses or volatility/open interest changes warrant
risk_framework.risk_model_used: Proprietary Risk Manager system; volatility forecasting model; mean-variance optimisation with correlation estimates

strategy.sub_strategy: Fundamental sub-sector equity market neutral
strategy.description: Fundamental equity market-neutral strategy organized around specialist sub-sector Portfolio Managers, each covering approximately 40–50 names with sole coverage. Bottom-up, fundamental research process focused on isolating idiosyncratic stock-specific alpha by hedging out systematic risks including style tilts, industry themes, and macro variables. Investment universe spans U.S., Asia (primarily Japan), and Europe across healthcare, technology, consumer, industrials, financials, and energy sub-sectors. Portfolio construction targets high idiosyncratic risk (80%+ at fund level) with limited net beta exposure. A center book (approximately 50% of risk) replicates PM positions to optimize gross exposure. Ideas have an average duration of approximately 3 months, generating approximately 2,000 annual ideas across the fund.
strategy.investment_thesis_core: Exploits idiosyncratic stock-specific mispricings within focused sub-sectors by combining deep fundamental research with quantitative risk management to isolate alpha from systematic factors, targeting a medium-term (~3 month) earnings-cycle horizon where human fundamental analysis has a competitive edge over both high-frequency quants and long-term investors.
strategy.idea_generation: Systematic research cycle including earnings season previews, post-earnings calls, monthly company interactions, conference seminars, industry events, and bespoke roadshows. PMs identify approximately 35 directional ideas within their coverage at any given time. Process evaluates: what matters to a stock's future performance, whether it is predictive, what is priced in, and whether the view is differentiated. Quantitative tools complement fundamental analysis. Position sizing determined by conviction, magnitude of differentiation vs. consensus, relative valuation, relative growth, residual stock performance, ability to hedge with other positions, and catalyst timing.
strategy.market_cap_focus: large cap and mid cap; primarily >$1bn
strategy.neutrality_approach: Beta neutral; limited net beta exposure; low factor exposure; each style and industry factor capped at 3% of risk
strategy.family_defining_note: Multi-PM platform structure with specialist sub-sector coverage; center book (~50% of risk) replicates PM positions; gross leverage target 250–300%; net exposure target +/-10% to +/-15%

risk_framework.risk_framework_description: Real-time risk management with daily risk reports and weekly review meetings. Capital allocation based on PM track record, sub-sector idiosyncratic volatility, and sub-sector liquidity. Sub-sector portfolio review triggered when performance deviates two standard deviations versus expectations (trailing 30-day). Hard limits: single-stock concentration capped at fund level; each style and industry factor capped at 3% of risk; idiosyncratic risk target minimum 80% at both PM and fund level. Gross leverage target 250–300%. Quantitative tools (Barra GEMLTL) used for factor risk monitoring. Crowding risk monitored via daily P&L correlation across sub-sector books (target under 5%). Trailing 12-month realized betas maintained below 0.02 to SPX, Russell 2000, NASDAQ, and MSCI ACWI.
risk_framework.drawdown_response_protocol: Sub-sector portfolio review triggered when performance deviates two standard deviations versus trailing 30-day expectations; triggers a conversation and re-underwriting rather than automatic capital reduction. Management committee determines capital allocation adjustments. No automatic stop-loss; capital cuts are discretionary based on skill assessment.
risk_framework.position_limits: Single-stock concentration: Top 5 positions 4–5% of GMV; Top 10 positions 6–8% of GMV; Top 25 positions 12–13% of GMV. Analysts: 1–4% of risk; PMs: 4–10% of risk; Co-CIOs: low double-digit % of risk.
risk_framework.sector_limits: Each style and industry factor capped at 3% of risk decomposition
risk_framework.stop_loss_policy: No pre-set stop-loss; 2 standard deviation trailing 30-day performance deviation triggers portfolio review and conversation

market_views.macro_thesis: Management believes the medium-term (~3 month earnings cycle) is the sweet spot for fundamental human analysis, avoiding both high-frequency quant competition at short horizons and unpredictable macro variables at long horizons. Approximately 40% of alpha is estimated to come in the 4 days around earnings. Retail investor activity creates volatility and opportunities. AI-driven narrative has created valuation dislocations in technology that the team views as fundamentally unjustified.
sector_views: Healthcare represents 40–45% of risk and has been the primary alpha driver historically; team has taken down some active risk there proactively
Technology is approximately 30% of risk; team has been fighting AI-driven valuation dislocations and momentum in tech

key_risks_identified: Crowding risk: management monitors daily P&L correlation across sub-sector books and tracks GS VIP and MS CRWD baskets
Factor risk: style and industry tilts can cause losses unrelated to fundamental stock selection
Healthcare concentration: 40–45% of risk in healthcare creates sector-specific event risk (e.g., binary readouts, takeouts)
Platform unwind risk: correlated de-grossing across multi-manager platforms can cause idiosyncratic losses
Capacity constraints: fund targeting hard close at $10–12 billion to preserve return quality and liquidity
market_views.forward_outlook: Management is focused on returning capital to bring hedge fund AUM back to approximately $10 billion from current ~$10.4 billion. Targeting 30 sub-sector portfolios total. Expanding into European consumer, US utilities, Japan industrials, and Japan healthcare. Woodline Spire (long extension product) targeting $10 billion AUM. Firm-wide AUM expected to reach approximately $20+ billion. Leverage target being raised toward 3–3.5x to support 10%+ net return goal.
